title: Sixth Word Five Degrees Of Profit From Selling The Trust

questions.question: What happens to things that do not stay forever when they are used for Allah?
What kind of life is talked about in the first gain: a life that stays here forever or a life that passes quickly?
When a person spends life for Allah, what comes from those moments later?
What is given as the great payment in the second gain?
In the third gain, what happens to the worth of a person’s body parts and senses?
What is one body gift used as the first example in the third gain?
If a person uses the mind only for selfish desires, what kind of burden can it bring?
What two time directions can trouble a person who misuses the mind?
What bad escape is mentioned for people who feel hurt by a misused mind?
If the mind is used for Allah, what does it become like?
questions.answer: A key that opens great treasures.

questions.question: What can the mind help a person get ready for when it is used the right way?
What sense is called a window for the soul?
If the eye is used only to chase passing beauty, what does it become low and dirty for?
If the eye is used for Allah and within His rules, what good job does it do?
questions.answer: It sees Allah’s signs and wonders.

questions.question: What two things are joined together in the next example after the eye?
If the tongue is used only for the stomach and selfish wants, what low job is it compared to?
If the tongue and taste are used for Allah, what do they become like?
questions.answer: A thankful inspector of Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: After the examples of mind, eye, and tongue, what are readers told to do with the other body gifts?
questions.answer: Compare them in the same way.

questions.question: What kind of nature does a believer grow by using Allah’s trust the right way?
What kind of nature does an unbeliever grow by misusing the trust?
Why does the believer receive a higher value?
questions.answer: Because he uses Allah’s gifts for Allah and within His limits.

questions.question: In the fourth gain, how is the human being described before trusting Allah?
questions.answer: Weak, needy, and full of troubles.

questions.question: What should a person do with Allah in the fourth gain to have peace?
questions.answer: Rely on Him and trust Him.

questions.question: What can happen inside a person if he does not trust Allah?
questions.answer: His heart and conscience stay upset.

questions.question: What might happen to a person who carries life’s weight without trusting Allah?
questions.answer: He may be crushed by pain or become like a beast.

questions.question: In the fifth gain, when will the reward of worship be given in a very needed way?
questions.answer: At the time of greatest need.

questions.question: In what form will that reward come?
Who agrees with this truth in the fifth gain?
questions.answer: People of deep faith who saw the truth clearly.

questions.question: How many gains are explained in the passage?
What is the first gain mainly about?
When life is given for Allah’s sake, does it become wasted or rewarded forever?
What picture is used for short life moments before they grow into reward?
What do those seed-like moments become later?
What reward is named in the second gain?
In the third gain, what happens to each body part and sense?
Which inner ability is described first in the examples?
If intelligence is used for the selfish self, what feelings can it load onto a person?
Why might a sinful person run to foolish fun or drink, according to the passage?
What does intelligence become when it is used for its true Owner?
questions.answer: A key to mercy and wisdom.

questions.question: What does good use of intelligence prepare a person for?
Which sense is described as helping the spirit look at the world?
What kind of things make the eye sink low if a person looks at them in a selfish way?
What does the eye become when it is used as Allah wants?
questions.answer: A viewer of Allah’s signs in creation.

questions.question: In the example of the tongue, what is wrong with using it only for eating pleasure?
questions.answer: It lowers the tongue to a very small job.

questions.question: What good rank does taste receive when it is used for Allah?
questions.answer: It becomes a thankful overseer of divine gifts.

questions.question: What do the mind, eye, and tongue examples teach about the other senses too?
questions.answer: They can rise or fall by how we use them.

questions.question: What makes a believer’s nature suitable for Paradise?
questions.answer: Using Allah’s trust in the right way.

questions.question: What makes an unbeliever’s nature suitable for Hell?
questions.answer: Misusing Allah’s trust for the selfish self.

questions.question: In the fourth gain, what three words describe people?
What heavy thing is mentioned in the fourth gain?
What gives relief from inner trouble in the fourth gain?
What bad results come if a person does not lean on Allah?
questions.answer: Torment, regret, and being dragged down.

questions.question: In the fifth gain, who agrees about the reward for worship?
questions.answer: Special people who were shown the truth.

questions.question: What parts of a person are said to worship and praise Allah?
When are the rewards especially given?
questions.answer: When a person needs them most.

questions.question: What are those rewards called in the passage?
What is the big idea of the first gain?
Who must life be given to for that lasting gain to happen?
If someone lives for Allah, do the moments disappear with no benefit or bring lasting blessings?
Besides the everlasting world, what other place is mentioned as receiving a bright side from those moments?
questions.answer: The world between this life and the next.

questions.question: What is the second gain in one short answer?
What is the main point of the third gain?
questions.answer: Human abilities become much more valuable.

questions.question: Which ability is compared to a useful tool?
When intelligence serves the selfish self, does it help peace or increase painful thoughts?
What two kinds of thoughts can misuse of intelligence bring?
What kind of person is said to look for unhealthy escape because of that pain?
What noble thing can intelligence become when it is used for Allah?
questions.answer: A guide leading to eternal happiness.

questions.question: What body part is called a window?
If the eye is used in a selfish way, what does it chase?
If the eye is used in a faithful way, what can it notice in the world?
What sense works together with the tongue in the next example?
Used wrongly, what low place is the tongue compared with?
Used rightly, what does taste become connected to?
What are readers asked to do after hearing these examples?
questions.answer: Think of the rest of the limbs in the same way.

questions.question: What does faith help a believer do with Allah’s trust?
What does an unbeliever do with that trust?
In the fourth gain, what is one reason people need Allah?
What should a person place in Allah in the fourth gain?
If a person does not trust Allah, what part inside stays disturbed?
What can unchecked pain and regret do to a person in the fourth gain?
Who are the people mentioned in the fifth gain as agreeing on this matter?
What actions of the body are mentioned there?
What will those actions become for the person later?
Why is the timing of that reward special?
questions.answer: It comes when the person needs it most.

questions.question: What change happens to temporary belongings in the first gain?
For whose sake must life be spent to receive that change?
Are life’s moments shown as useless trash or as something that can grow into reward?
questions.answer: Something that can grow into reward.

questions.question: What do those moments produce in the lasting world?
What precious exchange is named as the second gain?
In the third gain, what happens to the worth of a person’s limbs and senses?
Which example comes first: the ear, the mind, or the hand?
If the mind follows the selfish self, what does it become for the person?
What does that harmful use make a person remember and fear too much?
What does the passage say some sinful people use to dull that pain?
If the mind is used for Allah, what does it open?
What good future does rightly used intelligence guide a person toward?
What is the next body part explained after intelligence?
What lowers the eye when it is used for selfish wants?
What high work does the eye do when it is used within Allah’s limits?
questions.answer: It reads the signs in creation.

questions.question: What two things are taught together in the next example?
If they are used only for the belly, what do they become like?
If they are used for Allah, what quality do they show?
After these examples, what are we supposed to understand about all our other abilities?
questions.answer: They also rise or fall by our choices.

questions.question: What kind of person becomes fit for Paradise?
questions.answer: A believer who uses Allah’s trust rightly.

questions.question: What kind of person becomes fit for Hell?
questions.answer: An unbeliever who betrays the trust.

questions.question: In the fourth gain, what is man unable to handle well by himself?
What three actions toward Allah are named for peace in the fourth gain?
What can happen to a person who refuses this help from Allah?
questions.answer: He can be choked by pain and regret.

questions.question: In the fifth gain, whose agreement is mentioned?
questions.answer: The agreement of truthful spiritual people.

questions.question: What will be rewarded from a person’s members and instruments?
questions.answer: Their worship and praise of Allah.

questions.question: When will that reward come?
questions.answer: At the greatest time of need.

questions.question: What is the reward pictured as?
How does the passage describe the first benefit of giving oneself to Allah?
questions.answer: Short life becomes a source of lasting reward.

questions.question: What kind of Lord is mentioned in that first benefit?
What happens to the moments of life after they seem to pass away?
Where do those blessings bloom?
What is the second benefit that is given in return?
What is said about the value of the senses in the third benefit?
questions.answer: Their value grows many times over.

questions.question: Which human ability is the first example in that part?
What happens if intelligence is used for the selfish self instead of Allah?
What does this harmful intelligence fill a person with about yesterday and tomorrow?
What false relief may a sinful person try because of this pain?
What does intelligence become when it serves Allah?
questions.answer: A key to hidden treasures of mercy and wisdom.

questions.question: What does that good intelligence help lead to?
What sense is described next as a way for the spirit to look outside?
If the eye is used wrongly, what kind of things does it run after?
If the eye is used rightly, what does it become able to notice?
Which two are given as another example after the eye?
If the tongue is used just for eating and selfish wants, what low work is it compared to?
If taste is used for Allah, what kind of person is it like?
What should we do with the rest of our limbs after hearing these examples?
questions.answer: Judge them by the same rule.

questions.question: What gives a believer a Paradise-worthy character?
What causes an unbeliever to have a Hell-like character?
questions.answer: Using the trust for the lower self.

questions.question: In the fourth benefit, what is man like in front of many problems?
What must a person do to avoid a troubled inner life?
What can happen if a person carries life’s burden alone?
questions.answer: He may be crushed by pain and regret.

questions.question: According to the fifth benefit, who confirms the truth of this reward?
questions.answer: People who were given clear spiritual understanding.

questions.question: What things done by our limbs are rewarded?
questions.answer: Acts of worship and glorifying Allah.

questions.question: When will that reward be especially important?
questions.answer: When we need it the most.

questions.question: How is that reward described at the end of the fifth benefit?
What does the first profit say happens to things that do not last?
What must a person do with life for that to happen?
Are the moments of life truly lost when they are used for Allah?
What small thing is used to help us imagine life’s moments before they grow?
What big reward is named as the second profit?
What is the third profit about in a few words?
questions.answer: Our senses and limbs become far more valuable.

questions.question: What ability is the first example under this third profit?
If the mind serves the selfish self, what kind of tool does it become?
What two troubles can such a mind keep bringing back?
What might a sinful person seek to forget these troubles?
If the mind is used for Allah, what is it compared to?
What does that key open?
What happy end does such a mind prepare a person for?
Which sense is called a window for the spirit?
What happens to the eye if it is used only for selfish looking?
questions.answer: It falls to a low use.

questions.question: What good work does the eye do when used as Allah allows?
questions.answer: It observes Allah’s signs in the world.

questions.question: What two things are mentioned together in the last body-part example?
If they are used only for the stomach, what do they become like?
If they are used for Allah, what noble quality do they show?
What does the passage say to compare with these examples?
questions.answer: All the other limbs and tools.

questions.question: Why does the believer gain a value fit for Paradise?
questions.answer: Because he uses Allah’s trust within Allah’s limits.

questions.question: Why does the unbeliever gain a value fit for Hell?
questions.answer: Because he betrays the trust for the lower self.

questions.question: In the fourth profit, what is one truth about human beings?
What is another truth about human beings in that same part?
What should a person do with Allah so his conscience is not disturbed?
What can happen if he does not do that?
questions.answer: He can be filled with useless pain and regret.

questions.question: In the fifth profit, what group of people agree on the reward?
What will the worship done by our limbs become for us later?
questions.answer: Fruits of Paradise at the time of greatest need.
